_comment: The policy behind every control in this lab. Deliberately a file and not a constant in a function: a threshold you can read and change is a control you own. tune.py edits two of these; expert mode edits them with nano.

instruction_patterns.name: addresses the reader as a model

_instruction_patterns_note: PREVENT. inspect.py runs each pattern over every line of extracted text. These are somebody else's idea of what an instruction looks like, and OWASP LLM01:2026 prevention 3 says the quiet part: semantic filters are evadable by rephrasing. Write your own payload in expert mode and see.
_max_line_chars_note: PREVENT. No field on this invoice is longer than 44 characters. A line far longer than any field on the form is not a field. Measured: the doctored line is 82.
_visible_contrast_percent_note: DETECT. compare.py erases every mark fainter than this fraction of the brightness range before the visible-view OCR. Lab 4 measured the scale: 1.2% contrast is invisible on a screen, 29% is plainly visible. Measured on this invoice: the print sits at 92% contrast and the hidden line at 1.2%, so the mismatch holds from 2% all the way to 60% and there is no grey area to tune. Drop it below 1.2% and the hidden line counts as visible - the false negative. Push it past the print's own contrast and the print itself vanishes from the visible view - the false positive. Expert mode: move it and re-run compare.py on BOTH invoices.
_auto_accept_confidence_note: RECOVER. gate.py pays an ORIGINAL scan automatically when its confidence meets this; below it, the scan is held for a person. Shipped at 0.50, which is the vulnerable configuration: the perturbed stamp scores about 0.61 and goes straight to payment. tune.py raises it to 0.90. The clean duplicate scores 1.000 either way.
_your_indicators_note: Your own list, empty on purpose. tune.py adds the first words of the line your comparison caught. The four patterns above were written before your incident; this one exists because your own detector produced it.
